lina: Noticed a host-side P95 bump after we flipped the kernel selector to prefer_sparse_vec in canary-2026-03-24. GPU time dropped ~9% but host parse/tokenize tail increased ~18%.
omar: Any quick traces or syscall counts?
lina: Short perf capture (30s):
```
parse_reader.loop +40%
  -> http2::frame_decode +25%
  -> tokenize_pool::async_tokenize +15%
syscalls: readv/writev spikes, many 8-16B payloads
```
Batching median fell from 7->3. KV cache miss stable. Looks like selector choice changed batching window heuristics which fragmented gRPC frames.

jin: Repro on local harness: forcing legacy selector returns host P95 to baseline. Forcing sparse_vec keeps GPU win but host tail persists.
lina: I ran a tiny ablation: enabling sidecar coalescer (merge small writes up to 20ms or 256B) recovered ~12% of the host tail.
omar: Good signal. Two mitigations: 1) short-term sidecar coalescer behind flag + metric host_small_write_rate; 2) longer-term: add a selector->host hint (expected_frame_size) so batching heuristics adapt.

infra-bot: Canary run started id=canary-1911112222-01 collecting 8k traces; will post summary.

lina: I'll open PR for coalescer flag and add the small-write metric. Jin can you draft the selector hint proto?
jin: Yep, will sketch host_frame_hint in selector RPC and add examples (e.g., prefer_vec -> expect_frame<=64).
omar: Also experiment with TCP_CORK toggles in sidecar; helpful but needs guard for mixed payload sizes.
lina: Action items: PR for coalescer (WIP), selector hint proto, canary with coalescer. If canary restores SLO we avoid a rollback.

infra-bot: Canary summary id=canary-1911112222-01: end2end P95 +11% vs baseline, host parse P95 +18%, median batch size 7->3, syscall wakeups/request 1.0->2.8. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/canaries/1911112222-01/

lina: Thanks team. I'll post PR link when ready and keep canary running for another hour.
